gloss: formal kimono with family crest; crested garment

definitions.explanation: A formal Japanese garment featuring the wearer's family crest (mon). The most formal type of traditional Japanese attire.

examples.japanese: ⟦{結婚式|けっこんしき}→結婚式：05493_kekkonshiki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{紋付|もんつき}⟦{袴|はかま}→袴：02245_hakama⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}た→着る：00541_kiru⟧。
examples.english: I wore a crested kimono with hakama at the wedding.
examples.notes: {紋付|もんつき}⟦{袴|はかま}→袴：02245_hakama⟧ is the full formal outfit for men

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{紋付|もんつき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}け{継|つ}いだ→受け継ぐ：06700_uketsugu⟧。
examples.english: I inherited my grandfather's crested kimono.

examples.japanese: ⟦{五|いつ}つ→五つ：02892_itsutsu⟧⟦{紋|もん}→紋：13863_mon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{紋付|もんつき}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧⟦{格式|かくしき}→格式：16025_kakushiki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧。
examples.english: A crested kimono with five family crests is the most formal.
examples.notes: ⟦{五|いつ}つ→五つ：02892_itsutsu⟧⟦{紋|もん}→紋：13863_mon⟧ = five crests (the most formal level)

notes:
TRADITIONAL JAPANESE FORMAL WEAR:
{紋付|もんつき} refers to any garment bearing a family crest (⟦{家紋|かもん}→家紋：15366_kamon⟧). Most commonly refers to a formal black kimono worn by men at ceremonies.

FORMALITY LEVELS:
The number of crests indicates the level of formality:
- ⟦{五|いつ}つ→五つ：02892_itsutsu⟧⟦{紋|もん}→紋：13863_mon⟧ (5 crests): Most formal, for weddings, funerals
- ⟦{三|みっ}つ→三つ：02970_mittsu⟧⟦{紋|もん}→紋：13863_mon⟧ (3 crests): Semi-formal
- ⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦{紋|もん}→紋：13863_mon⟧ (1 crest): Less formal

FULL FORMAL OUTFIT:
For men: {紋付|もんつき}⟦{羽織|はおり}→羽織：05712_haori⟧⟦{袴|はかま}→袴：02245_hakama⟧ (crested haori jacket with hakama pants)
For women: ⟦{黒留|くろとめ}{袖|そで}→黒留袖：29520_kurotomesode⟧ with family crests

OCCASIONS:
- ⟦{結婚式|けっこんしき}→結婚式：05493_kekkonshiki⟧: Weddings
- ⟦{葬式|そうしき}→葬式：04389_soushiki⟧: Funerals
- ⟦{成人式|せいじんしき}→成人式：05494_seijinshiki⟧: Coming-of-age ceremony
- ⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧: Tea ceremony (formal occasions)

NOTE: Rental services (⟦{貸衣装|かしいしょう}→貸衣装：29519_kashiishou⟧) are common since many families no longer own {紋付|もんつき}.
